# What Honeycomb API keys the library redacts, and what it leaves alone.
#
# The exhaustive edges — every end of the alphabet, every count either side,
# every character a body excludes — are in builtin_honeycomb_api_key_test.go.
# What is here is the library end to end: the shapes a key is written in, the
# kinds the pattern reads and the ones it declines, and the collisions the
# grammar pays for.
#
# Every key here is built from the ordered run
# 0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz, which no real credential is, carrying on
# from 0 once the alphabet runs out. A body is letters and digits, so the run
# serves for it: once and a half over for the fifty-eight characters behind an
# ingest key's opening, and restarted at each half of a management key's, whose
# twenty-six and thirty-two the colon divides. With the six characters of an
# opening in front, an ingest key comes to sixty-four and a management key to
# sixty-five.

patterns: honeycomb-api-key

# The kinds of key that carry an opening and a secret behind it. Honeycomb
# writes the opening as hc, a character it assigns at key creation, two naming
# the kind and an underscore; the two ingest kinds concatenate the key ID and
# the secret, where a management key joins them with a colon. They are one
# pattern because a caller redacting what Honeycomb issues has the same reason
# for each of them, and no term of the vendor's covers two and leaves the third
# out.

case:     an ingest key in an environment assignment
in:       HONEYCOMB_API_KEY=hcxik_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcdefghijkl
out:      HONEYCOMB_API_KEY=«honeycomb-api-key»

case:     an ingest key in the header it is sent in
in:       X-Honeycomb-Team: hcxik_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcdefghijkl
out:      X-Honeycomb-Team: «honeycomb-api-key»

case:     a classic ingest key
in:       hcaic_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcdefghijkl
out:      «honeycomb-api-key»

case:     a management key in the header it is sent in
in:       Authorization: Bearer hcxmk_0123456789abcdefghijklmnop:0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv
out:      Authorization: Bearer «honeycomb-api-key»

case:     a key in the command line a request is made from
in:       curl -H 'X-Honeycomb-Team: hcxik_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcdefghijkl' https://api.honeycomb.io/1/batch/my-dataset
out:      curl -H 'X-Honeycomb-Team: «honeycomb-api-key»' https://api.honeycomb.io/1/batch/my-dataset

case:     the two keys a collector is configured with
in:       {"apiKey":"hcxik_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcdefghijkl","mgmtKey":"hcxmk_0123456789abcdefghijklmnop:0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv"}
out:      {"apiKey":"«honeycomb-api-key»","mgmtKey":"«honeycomb-api-key»"}

case:     a key followed by crlf
in:       X-Honeycomb-Team: hcxik_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcdefghijkl\r\n
out:      X-Honeycomb-Team: «honeycomb-api-key»\r\n

# The openings that carry no secret. Honeycomb writes one of the same shape in
# front of every resource it names — a team, an environment, a user — and a
# configuration key's opening stands in front of its key ID, which the vendor
# calls a label that identifies the key in its UI. So the two characters naming
# the kind are read as a table rather than as any two letters, and a key ID
# standing on its own is no value.

case:     a configuration key id with a body behind it
in:       hcxlk_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcdefghijkl
out:      hcxlk_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcdefghijkl

case:     the opening an environment identifier carries
in:       hcxen_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcdefghijkl
out:      hcxen_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcdefghijkl

case:     an ingest key id on its own
in:       key_id=hcxik_0123456789abcdefghijklmnop
out:      key_id=hcxik_0123456789abcdefghijklmnop

# The alphabet a key ID and a secret are written in: the letters of both cases
# and the digits. What it leaves out is everything else, the underscore an
# opening closes with among it.

case:     an uppercase body
in:       hcxik_0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKLMNOPQRSTUVWXYZ0123456789ABCDEFGHIJKL
out:      «honeycomb-api-key»

case:     a body carrying the separator
in:       hcxik_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrs_uvwxyz0123456789abcdefghijkl
out:      hcxik_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrs_uvwxyz0123456789abcdefghijkl

# The colon belongs to one kind alone. A management key's key ID and secret are
# joined by one; the ingest kinds write the two concatenated, and the colon is
# no character of a body.

case:     an ingest key written with a colon
in:       hcxik_0123456789abcdefghijklmnop:0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv
out:      hcxik_0123456789abcdefghijklmnop:0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv

case:     a management key written without one
in:       hcxmk_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcdefghijkl
out:      hcxmk_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcdefghijkl

# The counts either side. The fifty-eight a body comes to is what Refinery reads
# a whole ingest key's body at and what husky's sixty-four character classic
# ingest key leaves behind the opening; the twenty-six and the thirty-two are
# the key ID Honeycomb's OpenAPI states the width of and the secret its
# authentication page writes behind one. Each is used as a count rather than a
# floor: a body one character short is no key, and a body one character long is
# a key and one character that belongs to no credential. The second of those is
# the price of having no boundary behind the match — a boundary there would drop
# this key rather than trim it, and a real key written against a character of
# the same class would come through whole.

case:     a body of fifty-eight characters is a key
in:       hcxik_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcdefghijkl
out:      «honeycomb-api-key»

case:     a body of fifty-seven characters is not
in:       hcxik_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcdefghijk
out:      hcxik_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcdefghijk

case:     a run longer than a key is a key and what follows it
in:       hcxik_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcdefghijklm
out:      «honeycomb-api-key»m

case:     a key id of twenty-five characters is no management key
in:       hcxmk_0123456789abcdefghijklmno:0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv
out:      hcxmk_0123456789abcdefghijklmno:0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv

# What a key may be written against. The opening is the whole of the anchor and
# there is no boundary on either side of it, so a key keeps its span whatever
# word character it abuts.

case:     a key after an underscore
in:       HONEYCOMB_API_KEY_hcxik_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcdefghijkl
out:      HONEYCOMB_API_KEY_«honeycomb-api-key»

case:     a key at the end of a sentence
in:       the key is hcxik_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcdefghijkl.
out:      the key is «honeycomb-api-key».

case:     a key between multi-byte text with nothing between them
in:       キーはhcxik_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcdefghijklです
out:      キーは«honeycomb-api-key»です

# Two keys written together, and one written inside another. The last five
# characters of a body can spell hc, the assigned character and a kind, and the
# separator closing that opening is then the character written straight behind
# the key — so a key can begin five characters before the one in front of it
# ends. The two spans overlap and are redacted as one.

case:     two keys with nothing between them
in:       hcxik_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcdefghijklhcxmk_0123456789abcdefghijklmnop:0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuv
out:      «honeycomb-api-key»«honeycomb-api-key»

case:     a key whose last characters open another
in:       hcxik_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcdefghcaik_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcdefghijkl
out:      «honeycomb-api-key»

# The keys of this vendor's that carry no opening at all. A configuration key's
# Token is twenty-two characters of letters and digits and a Classic team's API
# key is thirty-two hexadecimal characters, both written with no prefix and no
# separator. Either is a word of an identifier, a git short SHA or an MD5, so
# nothing here reads them.

case:     a configuration key token in the header it is sent in
in:       X-Honeycomb-Team: 0123456789abcdefghijkl
out:      X-Honeycomb-Team: 0123456789abcdefghijkl

case:     a classic api key in an environment assignment
in:       HONEYCOMB_API_KEY=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      HONEYCOMB_API_KEY=0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

# And what a digest written behind an opening comes to. A SHA-256 is six
# characters longer than a body, so the first fifty-eight of one are a key here
# and the six behind them stay: fifty-eight characters of the body's own
# alphabet behind the vendor's own opening is a key's format exactly, and
# declining it would decline every key Honeycomb happened to write in the
# hexadecimal digits alone. A SHA-1 and an MD5 are short of the count.

case:     a sha-256 behind an ingest opening
in:       hcxik_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      «honeycomb-api-key»abcdef

case:     a sha-1 behind an ingest opening
in:       hcxik_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567
out:      hcxik_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef01234567

case:     an md5 behind an ingest opening
in:       hcxik_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef
out:      hcxik_0123456789abcdef0123456789abcdef

# And the shapes that reach the grammar nowhere.

case:     a body of the right length opening with no prefix
in:       0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcdefghijkl
out:      0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abcdefghijkl

case:     a key cut short with an ellipsis
in:       hcxik_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abc...
out:      hcxik_0123456789abcdefghijklmnopqrstuvwxyz0123456789abc...

case:     prose
in:       there is no credential in this sentence
out:      there is no credential in this sentence

case:     a log line naming the api a key authenticates against
in:       time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info msg="sending events" url=https://api.honeycomb.io/1/batch/my-dataset
out:      time=2026-08-17T00:00:00Z level=info msg="sending events" url=https://api.honeycomb.io/1/batch/my-dataset
